Stephanie O'Callaghan.b:
Stephanie O’Callaghan enters her sixth season with North Texas swimming and diving and serves as the Mean Green’s Associate Head Coach/Diving. Since joining UNT in 2021, O’Callaghan has transformed the Mean Green diving program into one of the most successful programs in The American, producing conference champions, record-setting performances, NCAA Zone qualifiers and the first NCAA All-American in program history.
Under O’Callaghan’s leadership, UNT has earned the most diving points of any school at the American Conference Championships in each of the last two seasons. In 2026, Mean Green divers captured six of the nine individual diving medals at the conference championships while also winning their second consecutive Team Diving championship. O’Callaghan was named The American’s Co-Diving Coach of the Year following the 2026 season after earning Diving Coach of the Year honors in 2025. UNT won silver in the Team Diving event in 2024 before capturing consecutive championships in 2025 and 2026.
In 2026, senior Kamryn Wong became the first diver in UNT history to qualify for the NCAA Championships and the first student-athlete in North Texas swimming and diving history to earn All-American honors. Wong earned NCAA Second Team All-American honors with a 16th-place finish on 3-meter, becoming the first Mean Green diver to score at the NCAA Championships. She finished her career as the program record holder on both 1-meter and 3-meter and was named The American’s Most Outstanding Diver in 2025 after sweeping the conference springboard titles.
O’Callaghan’s impact on the UNT record book reflects the depth and consistency of the program’s development under her leadership. During her tenure, all four diving school records have been broken and reset multiple times, with four different divers holding the platform record and three different divers holding the 3-meter record. Wong, Sydney Guidara and Amelia Sharp currently hold the program’s Team Diving record, which also stands as the American Conference record. Her divers account for six of UNT’s top 10 performances on 1-meter and seven of the top 10 on both 3-meter and platform, including the top six performances on platform.
UNT has also established unprecedented depth under O’Callaghan. The Mean Green have produced the largest number of NCAA Zone qualifiers in program history during her tenure, including a program-record five divers qualifying for Zones in a single season. In recent years, UNT divers have also competed at the AAU National Championships and USA Diving’s Spring and Winter National Championships. Guidara won both the 1-meter and 3-meter events at the AAU National Championships and advanced to the 1-meter finals at USA Diving’s Winter National Championships, finishing among the top 10.
The program has also produced the first individual medalists for UNT swimming and diving in each of its conference affiliations during O’Callaghan’s tenure. Saylor Hawkins became the first individual medalist in program history at the Conference USA Championships, earning bronze on 3-meter in 2022. In 2024, Sydney Guidara became the first individual medalist for UNT swimming and diving at The American Championships, earning silver on 3-meter. Guidara’s performance marked the program’s first individual medal as a member of The American.
Prior to North Texas, O’Callaghan coached at St. Bonaventure from 2016-21 after previously coaching the Bonnies from 2010-13. During her time at St. Bonaventure, all of the program’s men’s and women’s diving school records were broken before her departure. She earned Atlantic 10 Men’s Diving Coach of the Year honors in 2012, 2013 and 2021 and coached the Bonnies to the 2013 Atlantic 10 championship.
Between her two stints at St. Bonaventure, O’Callaghan served as the head men’s and women’s diving coach at the University of Findlay, where she coached two divers to the NCAA Division II Championships and helped establish new women’s diving school records.
O’Callaghan is a University of Michigan alumna and competed all four years as a member of the Wolverines’ swimming and diving program. She earned Academic All-Big Ten honors in each of her four seasons at Michigan. O’Callaghan also remains active in the sport as a Masters diver and has earned national titles in her age group.

Nick Wertz.b:
Nick Wertz was hired as an assistant coach on July 1, 2026, after serving as the head men's and women's coach at Malone University.
Wertz spent four years leading the men's and women's programs at his alma mater, which is an NCAA Division II university in Canton, Ohio.
In his time at the helm, Wertz developed and coached athletes to more than 100 Top-10 performances and three new program records.
As a student-athlete, Wertz excelled in distance events and was a 11-time Great Midwest Athletic Conference medalist, including one gold in the 1,650 Freestyle and he's the program record holder in the 1,650 Freestyle, 1,000 Freestyle and the 100 IM.

At UNT (9 years): 35-27
Brittany Roth was named the full-time head swimming and diving coach on April 11, 2017 by then-Vice President and director of athletics Wren Baker. She served as the interim head coach for the 2016-17 season.
Roth now enters her 10th season at the helm of the North Texas Swimming and Diving program. Roth has a dual record of 35-27 since taking over as full-time head coach prior to the 2017-18 season. During Roth’s time in Denton as head coach, more than half of the program's records have been topped at least once.
The 2025-26 season saw UNT earn its first All-American honor when senior diver Kamryn Wong was named a Second Team All-American after finishing in the top 16 at the NCAA Championships as the first diver in program history to qualify for the national meet. Prior to that, the Mean Green repeated as Team Diving champions at the American Conference Championships as the trio of Wong, Sydney Guidara and Amelia Sharp defended their title.
In 2024-25, the Mean Green had their best ever showing at the American Conference Championships with nine medals won at the meet, including its first three conference championships as a member of The American (team diving, 3-meter springboard, 1-meter springboard).
The 2023-24 season saw UNT earn its first conference championship medals as a member of the American Athletic Conference, as freshman diver Sydney Guidara won silver in the 3-meter springboard and was part of the new Team Diving event that shocked the meet with a silver medal performance along with Saylor Hawkins and Brigid Krbec. In the pool, junior Shaena McCloud earned the program's first swimming medal in the AAC meet with a bronze in 100 freestyle. The program sent three divers to NCAA Zones and five swimmers to the CSCAA National Invitational Championship.
In 2022-23, UNT ended up sending a trio of divers to the NCAA Zone Championships and seven swimmers to the CSCAA National Invitational Championship in its first season as a member of The American.
The 2021-22 season was UNT's final one in Conference USA and the team finished fourth at the conference championship thanks to a pair of bronze medals by the 400 freestyle relay team comprised of Shaena McCloud, London Farris, Bryanna Vasquez and Alvena Walpole and Saylor Hawkins in the 3-meter springboard diving competition.
The 2019-20 season saw North Texas push it’s home dual win streak to six straight including the Mean Green’s sixth straight dual win over the TCU Horned Frogs by the score of 161.5-138.5 on December 7. The Mean Green would finish fifth at the Conference USA Championships highlighted by a third place finish by the 800 free relay team made up of junior Leigh Faires McGee, sophomores Bryanna Vasquez and Alvena Walpole and freshman London Farris. North Texas qualified five student-athletes for the CSCAA National Invite that was ultimately canceled due to the COVID-19 outbreak.
In year three, Roth was named Conference USA’s Co-Coach of the Year after guiding North Texas to it’s highest winning percentage for dual meets in program history. The Mean Green went 6-2 in duals including two wins over Metroplex rival TCU. North Texas earned it’s highest finish at the Conference USA Championships, taking home third place as a team. The Mean Green took home seven medals and five school records. North Texas was one of 57 teams invited to the CSCAA National Invitational Championships where they finished 17th.
The 2018-19 team was honored out of the pool with four student-athletes receiving the C-USA Commissioner’s Academic Medal for achieving a 3.75 cumulative GPA or better, Brooke Beddingfield, Meghan Rousset, Kathleen Rousset and Brittany Thurstin all took home this honor. Another 20 student-athletes were named to the C-USA Commissioner’s Honor Roll.
During Roth’s second season at the helm, she coached CSCAA National Invitational Champion Claudia Kitching to gold in the 200 Breaststroke. Kitching’s performance at the CSCAA National Invitational set a meet and school record. North Texas finished fourth at the Conference USA Championships for a second consecutive season, taking home bronze medals in the 400 Medley and 400 Freestyle relays.
In its first season under Roth, the North Texas swimming and diving program saw several program firsts and new records set. The 2016-17 squad matched its highest finish (fourth) at the Conference USA Championships to date, having six members of the team medal in three different events. The squad finished the season 6-4 in dual meets, including a first-place showing at the Little Rock Invitational and a dual meet victory over TCU.
In one year under Roth, the Mean Green sent four swimmers to the USA Winter Nationals in Atlanta for the first time in program history. Additionally, five North Texas records fell under Roth’s leadership. North Texas posted five NCAA “B” standard times, had six swimmers land on the all-conference team, and continued to excel academically with a 3.15 team grade-point average, with seven student-athletes achieving a 4.0 and 17 above a 3.5.
Roth was named the interim head coach on July 1, 2016.
Roth spent three seasons an assistant coach at North Texas, having helped the Mean Green to a fourth-place finish at the Conference USA Championships, the best team finish since joining the league for the 2013-14 season.
The league championships capped one of the most successful seasons in school history, as they finished with the second-most dual-meet wins (7-4) and second-best winning percentage (.636) in school history.
Freshman Rebekah Bradley earned all-conference honors in the 100 backstroke and 200 backstroke, including a first-place finish in the 200 backstroke that is the first for the program since joining the league. Sophomore Claudia Kitching also earned all-conference honors in the 100 breaststroke and 200 breaststroke.
